A massive flash flood ripped through the Grand Canyon over the weekend, killing at least one person, leaving roughly 15 people missing or unaccounted for and knocking out the park’s water pipeline, according to news coverage.

The flooding struck Bright Angel Canyon on Saturday, forcing more than 60 people to be evacuated from Phantom Ranch and the lower North Kaibab Trail as rushing water destroyed footbridges and sent debris into the Colorado River, according to the National Park Service.

Officials recovered the body of a 46-year-old man Sunday evening near Crystal Rapids along the Colorado River, according to the Associated Press. Authorities did not immediately release additional details about his death. Severe flash flooding knocked out a central water line in the Grand Canyon this weekend, forcing the National Park Service to implement strict water restrictions amid an ongoing race to find missing hikers.

NPS says it will implement stage four water restrictions beginning at 12:00 p.m. on Monday, saying the Saturday flooding caused “extensive damage to infrastructure,” including the Transcanyon Waterline that supplies the park with water. Park officials say one person was killed and 15 may be missing after the flooding, though they say that is an estimate.

Park officials confirmed they recovered the body of a 46-year-old man from the Colorado River on Sunday night. He has not been publicly identified.

NPS issued a request for the public to provide information on the 15 other people who are believed to be missing.
